question: Can public collar knowledge provide a label-free tail behavior reference and improve synthetic-corruption robustness without sacrificing clean recognition?
corruption_units: Reconstruct g from normalized window times saved scale_g; corrupt in g, then repeat original per-window median-vector-norm normalization.
test_corruption_rng: Fixed global realization seed74103 per row, family and severity; independent of training stream; shared across all source types, source seeds, methods and endpoints.
bn_moments: Exact population variance over unlabeled training-window feature vectors; no gradients.
consistency: Teacher source fixed; student encoder/classifier/BN running statistics fixed, only16 BN affine parameters train. Teacher-clean vs student-corrupted KL + clean-anchor KL + affine-source L2.
selection: No confidence filtering, entropy-only objective, class balancing or test-based checkpoint/source/cow selection.
primary_metric: Equal-cow walking AP, after mean over3 source seeds per cow; primary comparisons at1000 on12 corrupted conditions and clean separately.
clean_retention_reporting: Always show clean AP change beside corruption AP change; no result-driven tolerance chosen.
scope_limits: Retrospective previously researched data, identities user-attested.
Three acceleration axes only; no hardware/9axis/crossspecies calibration validation.
Synthetic artifacts test response to specified corruption; no claim they reproduce actual observed hardware faults.
Training is label-free, final accuracy assessment requires held-out human truth.
No guarantee that more updates, higher confidence or consistency loss reduction means better behavior recognition.
